title: Consent text states a concrete personal-data processing purpose
pass_summary: Consent text contains a concrete personal-data processing purpose.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied consent text clearly states at least one concrete purpose for personal-data processing.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Consent to personal-data processing is separate from other terms
pass_summary: Consent to personal-data processing is presented separately from other terms.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied consent context shows that consent to personal-data processing is presented separately from accepting an offer, user agreement, or other independent terms. Treat the required element as PRESENT when the evidence shows a distinct personal-data consent control or distinct wording for personal-data consent, even if a separate offer or agreement control is nearby. Treat it as ABSENT only when the same control or same consent wording combines personal-data consent with accepting an offer, user agreement, or other independent terms. Do not treat the mere presence of a nearby offer link as ABSENT.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Consent text has a concrete and limited processing scope
pass_summary: Consent text has a concrete and limited processing scope.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied consent text contains a concrete and limited subject or scope of personal-data processing and does not use obviously unlimited wording such as 'any data', 'any purposes', or 'any actions' without limiting context. Treat the required element as PRESENT when the consent identifies a limited context such as a specific form, request, order, callback, account action, or named data categories/actions. Treat it as ABSENT when the consent is unlimited or open-ended by itself. Do not treat the word 'any' as ABSENT when the surrounding text clearly limits it to a concrete request, form, service, or legal context.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Marketing consent is separate from mandatory terms
pass_summary: Marketing consent is presented separately from mandatory terms.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied marketing or advertising consent context shows that consent to advertising or marketing messages is presented separately from mandatory consent to personal-data processing, contract acceptance, offer acceptance, user agreement, or other mandatory terms. Treat the required element as PRESENT when marketing consent has its own separate control or clearly separate optional wording. Treat it as ABSENT when the same mandatory control or same wording combines marketing consent with personal-data consent, contract, offer, user agreement, or other mandatory terms.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Privacy policy describes personal-data processing purposes
pass_summary: Privacy policy text describes personal-data processing purposes.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied privacy policy text describes purposes for personal-data processing. Treat the required element as PRESENT only when Evidence describes a concrete and understandable processing purpose that explains why personal data is processed, such as order processing, feedback, account registration or maintenance, providing a specific service, mailing/newsletter where stated, or reviewing a request. General wording such as 'for interaction with the site', 'for site operation', 'within the operator activity', or 'for other purposes' is too broad by itself and should not be treated as confident PRESENT; use AMBIGUOUS when wording looks purpose-like but remains too general.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Privacy policy describes categories of personal data
pass_summary: Privacy policy text describes personal-data categories.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied privacy policy text describes categories or examples of personal data being processed. Treat the required element as PRESENT only when Evidence names categories or concrete data types clearly enough to understand which data is processed, such as name/full name, phone, email, address, IP address, cookies/device identifiers, order data, or similar concrete examples. General wording such as 'user information', 'information provided by the user', or 'personal data necessary for service operation' is not sufficient by itself to describe categories; use AMBIGUOUS or ABSENT depending on the supplied text, but not PRESENT.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Privacy policy describes retention or deletion handling
pass_summary: Privacy policy text describes retention or deletion handling.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied privacy policy text describes retention periods, storage duration, deletion procedure, or conditions for ending personal-data processing.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.

title: Privacy policy describes data-subject request procedure
pass_summary: Privacy policy text describes a data-subject request procedure.

evaluation.criterion: Determine whether the supplied privacy policy text describes how a person can submit requests about their personal data, such as access, correction, withdrawal, blocking, or deletion requests.

remediation: Keep remediation in application logic; this shadow rule does not create user-facing findings.
limitations: Shadow-mode semantic pilot only. Does not create production Findings.
